confidence_notes: I used three web searches. One returned the RBA rate of 0.6720 USD per AUD for 18 November 2026. The search summary attributed this figure to the RBA exchange-rates page and its daily series; I did not open the page myself. To convert EUR to USD, I used about 1.10 USD per EUR, worked out from the AUD/USD and AUD/EUR rates in that summary (0.6720 and 0.6115). The restaurant, coffee and beer anchors come from 2026 aggregated cost-of-living data found by search. Expatica, citing Numbeo from June 2026, gives about EUR 13.5 for an inexpensive meal, about EUR 52 for a mid-range three-course meal for two, about EUR 3.1 for a 0.5 L domestic draft beer and about EUR 2.4 for a cappuccino. Hikersbay's figures are similar. I nudged these up slightly because July is peak season and tourist-area prices are higher. Cocktail and wine anchors come from travel guides and bar listings found by search, not price indexes, so they are less certain. Cocktails are mostly EUR 9-12 and wine by the glass mostly EUR 4-7, with natural-wine and rooftop bars charging more. All four accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge of Lisbon's July peak-season prices. I did not search them or check live listings. They are the least certain anchors and could be 20-30% off either way.
comparable_city_reasoning: I based the restaurant and drink anchors on Lisbon's own aggregated 2026 index data. As a check, I compared accommodation and drink levels with other Southern European capitals and tourist hubs, such as Porto, Madrid, Seville and Barcelona. Lisbon falls between Porto (cheaper) and Barcelona (dearer), and its July room rates are pushed up by strong tourist demand.
